newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Tenaga to reduce spending.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Tenaga to reduce spending.

text.p: Malaysia's dominant electric utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) plans to reduce its estimated annual five billion ringgit capital expenditure by 20 percent a year, local newspapers reported on Wednesday.

"From now on, TNB will practise prudent money management and trim its capital expenses by scrapping some of the projects based on necessity and profitability," Tenaga executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali was quoted as saying in the Sun newspaper.
He did not specify the projects, the newspapers reported.

"Ongoing expansion and upgrading projects will be maintained including the refurbishment of old substations. We are not cutting down, but we will be more prudent in spending," the Business Times quoted Ahmad Tajuddin as telling reporters.
Discussing Tenaga's recently priced $800 million Yankee bond offering, Ahmad Tajuddin said the company was seeking to raise another $200 million for capital expenditures.
"The balance can either be raised through Labuan or locally. But in which market, we cannot disclose yet," Ahmad Tajuddin said.
Tenaga officials could not immediately be reached for comment on Wednesday.
The latest Yankee bond offering was done through Labuan, a tax-haven off Borneo island set up by Malaysia in 1990 to compete with other similar financial centres.
